objective:
task Fix 5 founder-reported live product bugs on Muslim Rentals. Treat as live bugs, not new features. Each item below already has investigation findings from a pre-delegation repro pass -- use them as a starting point, but verify with real testing before shipping, per this repo's honesty-in-verification rules. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: Do NOT touch marker clustering/spiderfy logic (CLUSTER_OPTIONS, spiderfyOnMaxZoom, disableClusteringAtZoom, or the clustering/spiderfy behavior itself) in rentals/frontend/src/lib/mapMarkers.ts or rentals/frontend/src/components/map/FullMap.tsx. The founder has explicitly paused further work on that feature. Only touch marker VISUAL APPEARANCE (color/shape) per item 2 below, and only touch map lifecycle/cleanup per item 1 -- nothing about how clusters form or spiderfy. === ITEM 1: Map overlay persists after navigating away from /map === Founder report: after opening /map, clicking Login, Sign Up, or navigating elsewhere, the map remains visually rendered over the new page. Pre-delegation investigation (already done, do not repeat blindly): rentals/frontend/src/components/map/FullMap.tsx already has extensive unmount-cancellation guards (a `cancelled` flag checked at every async resumption point around the dynamic `import('leaflet')`, `map.remove()` in the effect cleanup, ResizeObserver disconnect, deleting the window.__mapListingClick bridge). Using Playwright against both the local dev server AND a local production build (`next build && next start`), I tested: (a) plain navigation Map->Browse, (b) navigation at delays of 0/20/50/100/200/500ms after mounting (racing the async Leaflet init), (c) opening the Login modal then navigating away while it's open, (d) full browser back/forward navigation chains. NONE of these reproduced a leftover `.leaflet-container` in the DOM. So the already-shipped lifecycle fix appears structurally sound against everything I could test locally. CRITICAL CONTEXT: this session discovered and just fixed a real Netlify production-build failure (`npm ERR! code ETARGET: No matching version found for fastq@1.20.2`, fixed in commit b730deb by pinning fastq to 1.20.1 via package.json overrides). Investigation shows the broken lockfile had been present on `main` since earlier today (confirmed via git blame/log: commit 6a844d6, well before this bug report), meaning Netlify builds were very likely failing silently for a meaningful stretch of today -- so production may have been serving a STALE build that predates the lifecycle fix (04b6f35) the whole time the founder was testing. This is a real possibility, not certain. What to actually do: (1) First have QA verify whether commit b730deb's Netlify build reached `ready` and whether the currently-live site actually contains the FullMap.tsx cleanup-guard code (e.g. check a fetched bundle for the `__leaflet_ro` / cancelled-flag pattern, or simply do a hard-refreshed live browser check of Map->Login/Sign Up/Browse/listing navigation on the actual production URL). (2) If the live, confirmed-fresh build still reproduces the bug, then dig deeper for a REAL remaining cause (e.g. z-index stacking against modals -- note Leaflet's own CSS sets `.leaflet-top`/`.leaflet-bottom` (zoom/attribution controls) to z-index:1000 while AuthModal and PostListingModal both use z-[100]/z-index:100, so Leaflet's controls could visually paint above a modal even though the map container itself is correctly clipped by its parent's overflow:hidden -- check whether this, or something else entirely, is the real live cause) -- do not just re-apply the same cancellation-guard pattern that's already there, since it already didn't reproduce locally. (3) If the fresh build actually fixes it (stale-build theory confirmed), no code change is needed for this item -- say so plainly rather than inventing a change to justify the task. Verify: Map -> Login, Map -> Sign Up, Map -> other pages (Browse, Home, a listing), on the actual production site once the live build is confirmed current. === ITEM 2: Marker appearance -- green bubble with price === Founder wants listing price markers on the map changed to a clear green bubble showing the price. Current code (rentals/frontend/src/app/globals.css, `.rental-marker` class) already renders a rounded pill at `background: #0a5c42` (a dark forest green) with the price as white text, built via `buildMarkerHtml()` in rentals/frontend/src/lib/mapMarkers.ts. This may already satisfy the ask once a fresh build is live (see ITEM 1's stale-build context) -- but treat this as a lightweight design polish regardless: have Designer confirm `#0a5c42` reads clearly as "green" at marker size on both light map tiles and dense clusters of pins, and adjust to a more vividly/unambiguously green tone if needed (e.g. brighten it, without touching clustering logic or marker sizing/touch-target CSS). Keep the price text clearly legible. Do not change marker size, touch target, or anything under CLUSTER_OPTIONS. === ITEM 3: My Listings -> clicking a listing crashes with "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred" === CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (verified by reading the actual backend code, not a guess): `GET /users/me/listings` in rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts (around line 128-137) returns the raw Prisma result directly (`res.json({ success: true, data: listings })`), without mapping `amenities` to a plain string array or including the `user` relation. Its Prisma query does `include: { images: { take: 1 }, amenities: { select: { name: true } }, _count: { select: { savedBy: true } } }` -- so each listing's `amenities` field comes back as an array of `{name: string}` objects, not strings. Compare to the CORRECT pattern already used elsewhere in the same file and in rentals/backend/src/routes/listings.ts: `GET /users/me/saved` (same file, ~line 95-125) does `amenities: s.listing.amenities.map(a => a.name)` and includes `user: { select: { id, name, avatarUrl } }`; `GET /listings` and `GET /listings/:id` in listings.ts do the same mapping and include `user` too. The frontend's shared ListingDetail.tsx component (rentals/frontend/src/components/listings/ListingDetail.tsx, ~line 139-146) renders `listing.amenities.map(a => {a})` assuming `amenities` is a string array. When `amenities` is actually an array of `{name}` objects, React throws "Objects are not valid as a React child" trying to render `{a}` -- this is the client-side exception, and it only shows on listings that have at least one amenity, which explains why it's not universal-feeling. Also: because `GET /users/me/listings` omits the `user` relation entirely, `listing.user` is `undefined` for every listing shown from My Listings, so ListingDetail's `isOwner = user?.id === listing.user?.id` check is always false for the founder's own listings viewed this way -- meaning the Delete button inside the detail modal wouldn't show, and the wrong "Message landlord" button would show instead, for the founder's own listing. Fix: in `GET /users/me/listings`, mirror the exact pattern already used by `GET /users/me/saved` two routes above it in the same file -- add `user: { select: { id: true, name: true, avatarUrl: true } }` to the Prisma `include`, and map the response to `data: listings.map(l => ({ ...l, amenities: l.amenities.map(a => a.name) }))`. Add a backend regression test for this route (there isn't one currently) asserting `amenities` comes back as `string[]` and `user` is present with `id`/`name`, so this exact class of bug (a "list my things" endpoint diverging from the shared listing-shape pattern used everywhere else) can't silently recur. Verify: log in, go to My Listings, click a listing that has amenities and confirm ListingDetail renders correctly (not a crash), confirm the owner sees "Delete listing" (not "Message landlord") in that modal, confirm a listing with zero amenities also still renders fine. === ITEM 4: Post Listing modal closes on accidental outside click, losing form data === CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE: rentals/frontend/src/components/listings/PostListingModal.tsx has, on BOTH its rendered variants (the not-authenticated prompt around line 101, and the main multi-step form around line 122), a backdrop `onClick={e => { if (e.target === e.currentTarget) handleClose(); }}` -- clicking the semi-transparent backdrop outside the modal card calls `handleClose()`, which resets the whole form (`reset(); setStep(1); setImages([]); setImagePreviews([]); setSelectedAmenities([]); onClose();`) and closes it, discarding all entered data. Fix: remove the backdrop-click-to-close behavior on both variants (delete the `onClick` handler on the outer `motion.div` backdrops, or make it a no-op). The modal should close ONLY via its explicit X button (already wired to `handleClose` at line 133) or the explicit "Cancel" button on the not-authenticated variant (line 108). Do not lose entered form data on an accidental outside click. Keep Escape-key-closes-modal behavior if that exists elsewhere in the app's modal conventions -- check other modals (AuthModal, ListingDetail, DeleteListingDialog) for the established pattern and stay consistent, but the outside-click-to-close specifically must be removed for PostListingModal per the founder's explicit ask. Verify: open Post Listing, fill in some fields, click outside the modal (on the backdrop) -- modal must stay open with the data intact. Click the X -- modal closes (data loss on explicit close is expected/fine). === ITEM 5: Photo upload is broken -- pressing upload submits the listing instead of letting the user upload a photo, and images never actually get saved === CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (part 1, definite): in `onSubmit` in PostListingModal.tsx (~line 68-83), the listing is always created with `imageUrls: []` hardcoded, with a comment "Images would be uploaded separately via /uploads endpoint" -- but nothing in this component ever actually calls that endpoint. Selected images live only in local `images: File[]` / `imagePreviews: string[]` state and are silently discarded on submit. This means NO image a user selects during posting is ever actually saved to a listing today, regardless of any click-handling issue. Existing backend infrastructure already supports this (do not build new infra, wire up what's there): `POST /uploads/listing-images/:listingId` in rentals/backend/src/routes/uploads.ts (requires an existing listing id, auth, ownership is enforced -- check the route to confirm), and the frontend already has a generic `api.upload(endpoint, formData)` helper in rentals/frontend/src/lib/api.ts (currently unused by PostListingModal). Fix: after `listingsApi.create(...)` succeeds and returns the new listing's id, build a `FormData` with the selected `images` files and call the upload endpoint (`api.upload` or a new `listingsApi`/`uploadsApi` wrapper around `POST /uploads/listing-images/:id`) before showing the success state and closing. Handle the case where image upload fails after the listing itself was created successfully (the listing should still exist; surface a clear, non-blocking error about the images specifically rather than losing the whole submission or leaving the user thinking nothing happened). CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (part 2, needs real-browser verification): the founder specifically reports that pressing the upload/photo control causes the listing to submit/post instead of opening the file picker. The dropzone control (react-dropzone's `getRootProps()`/`getInputProps()` on a `
`, around line 271-279) sits inside the same `
` as the final step-3 submit button. Static reading did not reveal an obvious way a click on that div would trigger form submission (it's not a submit button, and react-dropzone's default click handler just opens the native file picker) -- Frontend must reproduce this with a real browser/device click (not just code reading) to find the actual interaction bug, which could be an event-bubbling issue, a focus/keyboard-triggered submission, a mobile-specific quirk, or something not yet identified. Whatever the real cause turns out to be, fix it so clicking/tapping the upload control only ever opens the file picker or manages the drag-and-drop area, and never submits or navigates the form. Have Backend confirm the existing `POST /uploads/listing-images/:listingId` route's auth/ownership/file-type/size validation still holds (it should already enforce these -- do not weaken it), and have Security specifically review the wired-up upload flow (this repo's convention: Security reviews upload handling) for auth bypass, path traversal via filenames, oversized/wrong-type files, and ownership enforcement (a user must not be able to attach images to another user's listing via a manipulated listingId). Verify end-to-end: select an image during posting, confirm the picker opens (not a submit), confirm a preview appears, remove and re-add images, submit the listing, confirm the image is actually saved and appears on the resulting listing's detail page and in Browse/My Listings. === Process === Have Product/QA reproduce each issue against the actual current code (not just trust this brief) before signing off on a fix. Frontend owns items 1, 2, 4, and the client side of 5. Backend owns item 3 and the server side of 5. Designer reviews the UX of items 1, 2, and 4 (especially confirming the outside-click removal doesn't feel broken -- e.g. still allow Escape-to-close if consistent with other modals, and that there's no dead-end state). Security reviews the upload flow in item 5 specifically. Integrate all five fixes, run the full test suite plus typecheck plus a full clean production build (rm -rf node_modules, clean npm ci) before considering this ready to promote, add permanent regression coverage for all 5 flows (My Listings -> view listing detail renders without crashing regardless of amenities/owner; Post Listing modal survives an accidental outside click with data intact; image upload actually persists and appears on the listing), and report clearly per item 1 above whether that one turned out to need a code change or was actually a stale-build artifact -- do not fabricate a fix if real testing shows it already worked once the live build was current.
